title: Vinext upstream benchmark suite: native React and Redact

method.framework: Published vinext@1.3.0 with Redact maintained Vite compatibility transforms applied equally to both Vinext configurations; installed files unchanged
method.warmup: One untimed preflight per scenario and implementation
method.order: All six permutations of the three implementations, sequential; no concurrent benchmark builds or servers
method.bundleSizes: Measured from each of the six production builds
method.redact: Both configurations use redact() after vinext(); renderer is react for the native control and redact for the candidate
method.environment: Local workstation, not an isolated CI runner. Measured rounds run after the local compatibility and hosted verification processes finish. Per-sample load averages and free memory are retained.
method.security: Scoped Satori override to published fflate 0.7.5 in both Vinext configurations

provenance.workloadHashMethod: Sorted relative paths and file contents, separated by NUL bytes, SHA-256

statisticalMethod: Medians of six rounds. For timings, paired percentile bootstrap confidence intervals enumerate all 46,656 resamples of the six paired rounds. Local workstation noise and a small sample count limit generalization. No measurements are discarded.
limitations: This suite measures development cold starts, clean build time, and emitted compressed output. It does not benchmark browser render speed, hydration time, interaction responsiveness, production SSR throughput, LCP, or INP.

The client total sums all emitted JavaScript and CSS, including lazy routes. It is not the amount a browser downloads for one page. The client entry metric includes the browser entry and its eager static JavaScript imports.

Both Vinext configurations use native React on the server. Tiny server size changes can come from changed client chunk references and content hashes; they are not evidence of a server runtime optimization.
Next.js uses the upstream fixture pins, Next.js 16.2.7 and React 19.2.7. Vinext uses React 19.3.1. The direct Redact comparison uses identical Vinext dependencies and workloads.

The suite runs directly without CodSpeed profiling on a shared macOS workstation. Local compatibility and hosted verification finished before the measured rounds. Per-sample load averages and free memory are retained.
The Redact candidate is identified by the frozen tarball hash, not just its package.json version.

scenarios.label: Dev server cold start
scenarios.description: Time from launching a fresh dev-server process until the root route responds, with framework caches cleared before every round.

scenarios.label: Dev server cold start (large Pages Router app)
scenarios.description: Time from launching a fresh dev-server process until the root route of a generated Pages Router app responds. The app links 40 local packages through node_modules and imports them through barrel files (3,200 components). Framework caches are cleared before every round.

scenarios.label: Production build time
scenarios.description: Time to complete a clean production build with previous output removed.

scenarios.label: Client bundle size (gzip)
scenarios.description: Total gzip size of production client JavaScript and CSS emitted by the clean build.

scenarios.label: Client entry size (gzip)
scenarios.description: Total gzip size of the production browser entry and its eager static JavaScript imports.

scenarios.label: RSC entry closure size (gzip)
scenarios.description: Total gzip size of the vinext production RSC entry and its eager static JavaScript imports.

scenarios.label: Server bundle size (gzip)
scenarios.description: Total gzip size of production JavaScript and CSS emitted under vinext's dist/server directory, including the RSC entry, SSR entry, and shared chunks.
